newsitem.title: UK: Bell election papers accepted as UK independent.
newsitem.headline: Bell election papers accepted as UK independent.

text.p: BBC war reporter Martin Bell on Wednesday had his election nomination papers accepted to fight former Conservative minister Neil Hamilton in the Tatton constituency of north-west England, his campaign team said.

Bell decided to remove the "anti-corruption" label from the official documents to stave off any possible legal challenge from Hamilton, who denies claims that he took cash from businessmen to ask questions in parliament.
"Bell wanted to make sure that his nomination would not be rejected on legal grounds," said a spokeswoman for Bell.

The Labour and Liberal Democrat candidates have both stood down to clear the way for Bell to mount a direct challenge to Hamilton in the May 1 election. Bell will now be described merely as an independent.
